hypotheses.claim: The recent synchronous partner webhook call introduced in the consumer code (EV-CODE-001, EV-CODE-002) caused high HTTP latency, which inflated record processing time, exceeded max.poll.interval.ms, and triggered consumer lag spikes.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: Code diff adds a blocking HTTP POST with a 10 s timeout. Logs show processing latency jumped to 240 ms (EV-LOG-004) and poll interval exceeded (EV-LOG-002). Metrics record a processing‑time spike to 310 ms (EV-MET-002) and webhook latency spike to 305 ms (EV-MET-003). Correlation between processing time and webhook latency is near‑perfect (EV-MET-005), linking the new call to the slowdown that caused lag (EV-LOG-001, EV-MET-001).
falsification_criteria: If the partner webhook latency remains below 50 ms while consumer lag stays above the critical threshold, the hypothesis is disproved.
verification_plan: Instrument the consumer to log webhook response times per request.
Temporarily disable the synchronous webhook call and measure processing time and lag metrics.
Compare poll interval violations before and after disabling the call.
Confirm that lag returns to baseline when webhook latency is low.

hypotheses.claim: A poll timeout (max.poll.interval.ms) on worker‑2 caused a rebalance storm, removing the worker from the consumer group and leading to a sudden drop in consumption rate and lag accumulation.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: Logs record a poll interval exceedance (EV-LOG-002) followed by a rebalance storm that kicked worker‑2 out (EV-LOG-003). Subsequent logs show critical lag (EV-LOG-001). Metrics show lag records surged to 140k (EV-MET-001) while consumed records per second fell to 8 (EV-MET-004), consistent with a consumer being removed from the group.
falsification_criteria: If no poll timeout events are observed in the Kafka client metrics during the lag period, this hypothesis is falsified.
verification_plan: Query the Kafka client metrics for max.poll.interval.ms violations during the incident window.
Inspect the consumer group state to verify whether worker‑2 was removed and later rejoined.
Correlate timestamps of poll timeout, rebalance, and consumption‑rate drop.

hypotheses.claim: A broker‑side partition balance advisory (EV-LOG-005) led to uneven partition assignment, causing one consumer to be overloaded and generating the observed lag.
hypotheses.supporting_reasoning: The broker logged a partition balance advisory (EV-LOG-005) shortly before lag metrics spiked (EV-MET-001) and consumption rate collapsed (EV-MET-004). An uneven partition distribution could overload a consumer, producing backlog and lag.
falsification_criteria: If partition assignment logs show balanced distribution across consumers during the lag period, this hypothesis is disproved.
verification_plan: Retrieve the partition assignment snapshot for the consumer group at the time of the lag.
Check broker logs for any subsequent rebalancing actions that corrected partition imbalance.
Verify that consumption rates per partition are uniform after the advisory.
